sections.text:
¹ De Toz cf. supra p. 98, n. 2. — Libri quos Albertus inspexit iam periisse
videntur.
² Scripta magica vel astrologica Salomonis medio quod dicitur aevo multa
ferebantur; vide e. g. Kroll, Catal., VI, p. 85. Quinquaginta in uno codice Bod-
leiano invenit Steinschneider, l. c., p. 386, 32, sed paucissima de libris ab Alberto
memoratis dicere valuit.
³ Arabes multos habent libros de Dei nominibus; versio latina iam servari non
videtur. Cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 375, § 35.
sections.en:
¹ Concerning Toz cf. supra p. 98, n. 2. — The books which Albertus inspected seem to have already
perished.
² Many magical or astrological writings of Solomon were circulated in the so-called Middle
Ages; see e. g. Kroll, Catal., VI, p. 85. Steinschneider found fifty in one Bodleian
codex, l. c., p. 386, 32, but he was able to say very little concerning the books mentioned by Albertus.
³ The Arabs have many books concerning the names of God; the Latin version seems no longer to be
preserved. Cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 375, § 35.

summary.headline: Astrological and Magical Books
summary.text: Catalog of astrological and magical writings attributed to Hermes, Toz the Greek, Solomon, and Mahomet, including books on planetary images, the seven planetary rings, Venus stations and mirrors, Solomon’s rings and spirit figures, Almandal, demonic seals, and the seven names.
